original_question: Determine whether there exists a II1 factor N such that the 1-bounded entropy h(NU) of its ultrapower is infinite while h(N) = 0.
target_in_paper: Problem 40 in the section "Miscellaneous": the paper asks whether there exists a II_1 factor N with h(N^{\mathcal U}) = \infty and h(N) = 0, where \mathcal U is the fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter on \mathbb N used throughout the paper and h denotes 1-bounded entropy. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical phenomenon asked about in the paper: an existence question for a II_1 factor, comparing the 1-bounded entropy of the factor itself with that of its ultrapower, with the specific target values h(N) = 0 and h(N^{\mathcal U}) = \infty. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
missing_details: The ultrapower is specifically the tracial ultrapower N^{\mathcal U}, not an arbitrary ultrapower; this comes from the global notation fixed immediately after the abstract. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
The ultrafilter \mathcal U is fixed throughout the paper and is assumed to be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on \mathbb N. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
The notation h is explicitly the 1-bounded entropy; the paper also identifies Hayes's work as the reference for this notion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

Problem 40 imposes no extra hypotheses beyond N being a II_1 factor; in particular, the paper does not add separability, Connes embeddability, fullness, or group-measure-space assumptions here. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

To match the paper exactly, the question should be phrased as the narrow existence problem "Does there exist ...?" rather than a broader request to classify or otherwise determine the general behavior. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
refined_question: Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter \mathcal U on \mathbb N, and let N^{\mathcal U} denote the tracial ultrapower of a II_1 factor N. Does there exist a II_1 factor N such that its 1-bounded entropy satisfies h(N) = 0 while h(N^{\mathcal U}) = \infty? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 40 exactly: in the paper's "Miscellaneous" section, Problem 40 asks for the existence of a II_1 factor whose own 1-bounded entropy is 0 but whose tracial ultrapower has infinite 1-bounded entropy. The only hidden assumptions needed to make the question stand alone are supplied by the notation paragraph after the abstract, which fixes \mathcal U as a nonprincipal ultrafilter on \mathbb N and defines N^{\mathcal U} as the tracial ultrapower. The paper does not state any equivalent reformulation of this problem nearby, so the faithful rewrite is simply the original existence question with those ambient conventions made explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
